sections.html:
New Milford, in Litchfield County, is the largest Connecticut town by land, with 61.6 square miles. It lies about 14 miles north of Danbury on the Housatonic River and belongs to Greater Danbury and the New York metropolitan area. The 2020 census counted 28,115 residents, and the 2024 estimate is 28,334.

A town this wide has long drives between its parts. A house on a farm road in Merryall is a very different sale from one near the green, so describe the setting as well as the structure.

No single neighborhood system exists here. Instead the town has named communities scattered across it: New Milford Center, Gaylordsville, Northville, Still River, Lanesville, Merryall (upper and lower), Merwinsville, Chimney Point, Park Lane, Candlewood Hills, Sunny Valley, Pickett District and Squash Hollow.

  • Gaylordsville has its own ZIP code, 06755. The rest of town uses 06776.
  • Most roads branch off U.S. 7 and U.S. 202, which cross and split inside town.
  • Communities on Candlewood Lake's northeast corner, and the rural land between Routes 7 and 202, see more visitors from May to October.

Knowing which village your house belongs to helps a buyer picture the commute and the setting. Some of the oldest housing stands near the New Milford Center Historic District, which takes in Bennitt, Elm, East, South Main, Mill and Railroad streets and is on the National Register.

The town lies on the northeastern shore of Candlewood Lake, and the East Aspetuck, Still and Housatonic rivers all run through it. A few local offices handle questions about water.

  • Candlewood Lake Authority: 860-354-6928.
  • Inland Wetlands: 860-355-6083.
  • Health Department and sanitarian: 860-355-6035, the number to call about septic.

Own near wetlands, a river or the lake? Ask these offices what a buyer would need to know, and write down the answers.

Winter is hard on older houses here. An aging oil or propane system, a tired roof or a wet basement are the repairs that come up most often in a Litchfield County sale, and a cash buyer will not make you fix them first.

New Milford runs on a mayor-council system with a nine-member Town Council. The town has also built a 1,000,000-gallon sewer plant expansion on West Street, so the WPCA is the place to learn whether your address is on sewer.

Under state law the seller normally settles the tax balance through the closing. Late municipal tax carries 18 percent annual interest, which is 1.5 percent per month with a $2 minimum per installment (C.G.S. 12-146).

Call the Tax Collector at 860-355-6085 for the installment dates and the figure you owe, and the Assessor at 860-355-6070 about your assessed value. Ask for the payoff to be good through your closing date so the closing attorney can pay it from the proceeds.

Connecticut charges a conveyance tax on each deed, and the seller's side handles the return. The base is three-quarters of one percent to the state and one-quarter of one percent to the town.

  • On a residential price above $800,000, the state charges a higher rate on the excess.
  • Form OP-236 goes to the town clerk at recording, and the tax is paid then.
  • Targeted investment communities may add up to one-quarter of one percent.

The Town Clerk can confirm the rate that applies to your sale.

Housatonic Area Regional Transit runs buses, and U.S. 7 and U.S. 202 are the main roads. Metro-North's Danbury Branch ends in Danbury. Tracks north of there carry freight only, and passenger service north has been discussed for years but does not exist.

The New Milford School District operates Hill and Plain, Northville, Sarah Noble Intermediate, Schaghticoke Middle and New Milford High School. Canterbury School, a Catholic boarding school, is also in town.

sections.h2: Wells, septic and heating on a larger lot
sections.html:
On a big rural lot, buyers fixate on three systems: where the water comes from, where the waste goes and what keeps the house warm. If you have a well, find the most recent water test. If you have a septic system, find out when it was last pumped and where the tank and field sit. If the house burns oil or propane, note the tank's location and age. A seller who can answer these quickly looks organized, and a seller who cannot should be ready to have the buyer price in the unknowns.

With a cash sale there is no inspection-driven repair list from a lender, but an honest description still prevents a late renegotiation.

The choice is between a traditional listing and a direct cash sale, and it turns on the condition of the house and your timing.

  • A listing brings showings, a buyer's inspection and perhaps lender-driven repair requests.
  • A cash sale lets you skip repairs and pick the closing date.
  • An inherited or rural house that needs work often suits the second route.

Cash Home Buyers buys houses in New Milford in any condition. Tell us about the property and we will send an offer you can compare.

sections.h2: What a cash sale leaves out
sections.html: A financed buyer usually needs an appraisal, a lender's underwriting and a mortgage commitment before closing, and a problem at any of them can delay the date or lower the price. A cash buyer has none of those. You also avoid photographs, staging and weekend showings, which matter when the house is far from town or sits empty. What you give up is the chance to wait for a retail buyer, so compare the written offer with what a listing would net after repairs, commission and carrying costs.

1. You accept an offer and choose a closing date.
  2. A title company or attorney orders the title search and asks your mortgage lender for a payoff letter.
  3. The Tax Collector provides the tax balance, and the WPCA confirms any sewer charge.
  4. You sign the deed, the OP-236 return and tax go to the Town Clerk, and the deed is recorded.
  5. Taxes and payoffs are subtracted from the proceeds, and you get the balance.

Bring photo ID and your latest mortgage and tax statements. For a rural house, gather what you know about the well, the septic system and the heating fuel, since a buyer will ask. If the house is an inheritance, confirm who has authority to sign before a date is set. Take your belongings out before the walk-through, and keep your insurance active until the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Is New Milford the largest town in Connecticut?
faqs.a: By land area, yes. It has about 61.6 square miles of land.

faqs.q: How do I find my New Milford tax balance before closing?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Collector at 860-355-6085. The office can give the amount owed so it is paid at closing.

faqs.q: Is there a conveyance tax when I sell in New Milford?
faqs.a: Yes. The base is three-quarters of one percent to the state and one-quarter of one percent to the town. The Town Clerk can confirm whether an extra municipal rate applies.

faqs.q: Can I sell a lakeside house near Candlewood Lake as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases it in its current condition. The Candlewood Lake Authority and the Inland Wetlands office can answer waterfront questions.

faqs.q: Is there commuter rail in New Milford?
faqs.a: No. Metro-North's Danbury Branch ends in Danbury, and the tracks north of it carry freight. Local buses are run by Housatonic Area Regional Transit.
